intent: Answer the question the campaign has been working around for three sessions: is rpi_nc_install.sh's 11.36% a testing gap or an instrument failure? Proven to be the latter, against an independent instrument, and the kcov problem is now split into two defects with different fixes.
scope: docs/kcov-under-report.md: new, split out of shell-split-verification.md for the 250-line cap
docs/shell-split-verification.md: the kcov section replaced by a pointer
NEXT_SESSION_PROMPT.md: rewritten to lead with the instrument work
Non-goal: fixing either defect -- this commit establishes WHICH defect is which, so the next session does not fix the wrong one
changes: MEASURED, not hypothesised: driving rpi_nc_install.sh directly under PS4='+PS4:${BASH_SOURCE##*/}:${LINENO} ' with set -x traces 55 distinct lines as executed, and 45 of them are lines kcov reports as uncovered -- including 61, 62, 63, 66, 68, 102, 118 and 146. The lines run; kcov does not record them.

This splits the problem in two. (a) WRONG DENOMINATOR: continuation lines of a multi-line quoted argument counted as statements, which a bash -x tracer never calls executable -- fixable in shell_coverage_report.py, and it is what holds dwm_config.sh down. (b) WRONG NUMERATOR: ordinary statements executing unrecorded, which is what caps rpi_nc_install.sh and which no test can move.

The distinction matters because a denominator filter -- the obvious fix, and the one I nearly built last session -- does nothing for (b). Knowing which defect a lib suffers from tells you whether writing tests can help it.

Confirmed no test can raise rpi_nc_install.sh: the file is ONE 227-line function, called twice, and an `exit 88` sentinel proves the suite runs to completion with all 29 assertions passing. Its assertions on save_config (line 219) and the password message (line 227) PASS while kcov calls both lines uncovered.

verification.command: minimal repro: perl -0777 block under kcov, then the same file under PS4='+LINE:${LINENO} ' bash -x
verification.evidence: kcov reports lines 6,7,8 as instrumentable with hits=0; the PS4 tracer never emits them at all. Establishes defect (a) as a denominator error rather than a missed execution.

verification.command: drive rpi_nc_install.sh's phase_install_nextcloud under PS4 with every external stubbed, outside the jail
verification.evidence: 55 distinct lines traced, max line 166. Spot-checked against kcov's uncovered list: 61, 62, 63, 66, 68, 102, 118, 146 all SEEN EXECUTING. 45 of kcov's uncovered lines appear in the PS4 set. Establishes defect (b).

verification.command: append `exit 88` before _t_report in test_rpi_nc_install.sh, run under --fail-on-case-error, restore
verification.evidence: 'case exited 88' fired: the suite reaches its end with all 29 assertions passing. Combined with the PS4 trace, this rules out 'the tests do not exercise the code' as an explanation.
kcov 43, which is the current release in extra/. Upgrading is not an available fix.

verification.command: bash meta/scripts/check_file_length.sh --all after the doc split
verification.evidence: all files within 250 lines: shell-split-verification.md 173, kcov-under-report.md 99, NEXT_SESSION_PROMPT.md 173.

risks: The PS4 measurement ran OUTSIDE the jail with a simplified fixture, so it reached line 166 and returned 1 rather than running the full 227 lines. That is sufficient for the discriminating question (do lines kcov calls uncovered execute at all?) but it is not a full-coverage figure and must not be quoted as one.

Replacing kcov's numerator with a PS4 tracer is a bigger change than a denominator filter and could introduce its own inaccuracies. The acceptance test is recorded in the handoff: dot_resolver_install.sh must stay at 39/39 and rpi_nc_ca.sh must not fall below 98.63%.
rollback: git revert the commit; the kcov material returns to shell-split-verification.md and the handoff loses the (a)/(b) split.
After rollback, confirm shell-split-verification.md is back over 250 lines -- that cap violation is why the split happened.
